question: Why did diluting the amines with more water raise the CO2 capture efficiency in System 1, the CO2 jet?
expect: premise false: in System 1 more water did not help; both amines were best at 1:1 and efficiency fell with further dilution (the water benefit is System 2's) (sec. 3.1)
rendered:
Evaluating CO2 Capture in Aqueous Amine Solution by Using a New Microbubble System, page 6

The dilution of amines with more water raised the CO2 capture efficiency in System 1, the CO2 jet, because of the hydration reactions leading to bicarbonate formation. The presence of water improved CO2 uptake through hydration reactions, which slightly increased the overall CO2 capture capacity. This contribution is limited but can slightly increase the capture efficiency.
